D: A shy Paris waitress secretly sets out to improve the lives of the people around her.
P: Serve dessert when Amélie cracks the top of her crème brûlée with a spoon.
S: the crates outside Monsieur Collignon's grocery
Crisp radishes with their leaves on, served with soft butter and flaky salt for dipping, beside a pile of baby carrots.
the Café des 2 Moulins in Montmartre
Baguette slices toasted and topped two ways: brie with fig jam, and ham with Dijon, laid out on a wooden board.
Amélie skipping stones on the Canal Saint-Martin

Potatoes sliced paper thin on a mandoline, fried until crisp and tossed with thyme salt and lemon zest, with a garlicky aioli for dipping. Slice 3 large washed potatoes 1 to 2mm thick on a mandoline. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes, drain and dry very well on tea towels. Heat oil in a deep saucepan to 170C and fry in small batches for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden. Drain on paper towel. Crush 1 tsp sea salt with 1 tsp thyme leaves and the zest of half a lemon and toss through. Stir a crushed garlic clove into 150g mayonnaise for the aioli.
M: Chicken thighs browned and braised with white wine and mushrooms for 40 minutes, finished with cream, served with buttery mash.
the café in Montmartre where Amélie waits tables

Ham and gruyère between slices of white bread, spread with béchamel, grilled until bubbling and blistered, topped with a runny fried egg and chives. Make béchamel: melt 30g butter, stir in 30g plain flour for 1 minute, whisk in 300ml milk and simmer 3 minutes until thick, then add nutmeg, salt and 40g grated gruyère. Spread 8 slices of white bread with Dijon, fill 4 sandwiches with 200g ham and 120g gruyère. Toast in a buttered pan 3 minutes a side. Spread the tops thickly with béchamel, add more gruyère and grill at 220C for 4 minutes until blistered. Top each with a fried egg and chives.
W: Amélie cracking the burnt sugar with her spoon
Vanilla custard baked in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes, chilled, sugar scattered on top and torched until it sets hard.
K: the regulars at the Café des 2 Moulins

Crème de cassis poured into chilled flutes and topped slowly with cold dry sparkling wine, finished with a fresh raspberry or blackberry dropped in. Chill 4 champagne flutes and a bottle of dry sparkling wine for at least 2 hours. Pour 15ml crème de cassis into each flute. Tilt the glass and top slowly with the sparkling wine, about 120ml each, so the cassis rises through it and turns the glass a deep pink. Drop a raspberry or blackberry into each and serve straight away. For non-drinkers, top cassis cordial with soda water instead.

s.note: the crates outside Monsieur Collignon's grocery
s.how: Wash a bunch of radishes, leaving the leaves on, and pile them on a board with baby carrots. Set out a dish of soft butter and a pile of sea salt flakes. Swipe each radish through the butter, then dip in the salt.

s.note: the Café des 2 Moulins in Montmartre
s.how: Slice a baguette and toast until golden. Top half with brie and a spoon of fig jam. Spread the rest with Dijon and top with folded ham. Lay them out on a wooden board at a small Montmartre cafe.

m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden. Pour in 250ml white wine and simmer 30 minutes, then stir in 150ml cream. Serve over buttery mash from 1kg potatoes. Small pleasures.

w.note: Amélie cracking the burnt sugar with her spoon
w.how: Heat 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean. Whisk 6 yolks with 80g sugar, pour in the cream and strain into ramekins. Bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes and chill. Sprinkle with sugar and torch. Crack the top with a spoon.
